-----Original Message-----
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: FoldHealth trial — schedule & capacity run-through for hands-on session

Hi Samira —
Thanks for sending the product mapping. We want to make the first hands-on session as productive as possible. Proposed plan:
1) 30m kickoff (intro, success criteria, network/KMS check)
2) 90m hands-on: prompt review + routing test (prefix caching + fallback routing)
3) 60m load window: focused token burn/load test with our dedicated harness

Quick answers to your asks:
- Token budget: baseline Hosted trial gives ~1.5M tokens/day. For the load window (20 concurrent users) we recommend a bump to 8M tokens/day or a short Dedicated carve (2x capacity) for the week.
- Lead time: Hosted quota bumps can often be provisioned same-day if under 10M tokens. Dedicated capacity requires contract commit and 48–72 hours for allocation.
- Prep: please share representative prompts and any sensitive data constraints. We can pre-stage caches for repeated prompts to show cost/latency delta.

Availability: Jan 6–12 we have several 2–3 hour slots. If you share preferred times, we’ll lock one.

— Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FoldHealth trial — schedule & capacity run-through for hands-on session

Samira —
Quick note on routing/load specifics so scheduling aligns with infrastructure:
- For the hands-on, Priyom will lead routing demo: show live fallback from high-performing open model to quantized variant during a synthetic latency spike.
- For the load window, we’ll need a one-hour warmup (low concurrency ramp) so KV caches fill. Plan adds ~15% headroom to tokens consumed during the peak hour.
- If you expect long context runs (2k+ tokens) let us know — that changes kernel selection and token counts.

I can join the Jan 7 afternoon slot or Jan 10 morning.
— Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Samira — tagging in the capacity matrix (attached). It maps Hosted token ceilings, short-term bump policies, and Dedicated carve timelines. Highlights:
- Hosted same-day bump: up to +10M tokens/day for trials (subject to security checks).
- Emergency SLA: if a production incident necessitates, we can provision burst capacity within 8 hours but requires approval from billing (we’ll signal).
- Dedicated trial: estimate 48–72 hour lead time for GPU pool assignment; recommend if you plan sustained load for >5 days.

Samira — great session today. Quick recap and next steps (action items):
1) Session summary: prompt review, routing fallback demonstration, and a one-hour focused load window. Peak token burn measured ~1.8M tokens in the hour after warmup (consistent with our warmup estimate).
2) Capacity: Hosted bump remained sufficient for the trial — no Dedicated carve required. We left a 25% headroom buffer configured for Jan 9–12.
3) Follow-ups:
   - Priyom: capture routing config used and share as a runnable snippet (GH gist). Due Jan 13.
   - Evelyn: file a temporary invoice/usage note for trial bump so billing can reconcile. Due Jan 14.
   - Michael: schedule a 30m readout with FoldHealth execs to discuss production assumptions (week of Jan 18).

Attachments: test logs and the capacity snapshot are in the shared Drive (links on the calendar event).

Thanks everyone — the prompts from your QA team were very helpful and the routing tests showed clear latency savings when caches hit.

— Michael
